# MonoDreams Blocks

The engine ships as a set of **blocks** — self-contained, copyable
slices of source code. Each block is a directory under `MonoDreams/`
with its own `block.json` manifest sitting next to the code it
describes. The `monodreams` CLI reads these manifests, resolves the
dependency graph, and copies the source into a user's project.

The model is **shadcn for C# game code**: nothing is hidden behind a
NuGet binary. The user owns every line; AI agents can read and edit
the code in place.

## Layout

```
MonoDreams/
  block.schema.json       ← JSON Schema validating every manifest
  presets.json            ← curated block combinations
  BLOCKS.md               ← this file
  MonoDreams.csproj       ← engine project (globs all block source)
  README.md, Icon.*       ← engine-only project assets
  Effect/                 ← engine-only shaders (not part of any block)
  <block>/
    block.json            ← the manifest
    ...source files...    ← all files inside ARE the block
```

The 13 blocks:

```
foundation              (required base — installed by `monodreams init`)
├── rendering            (includes mesh primitives — IMeshGenerator, MeshData)
│   ├── rendering-text
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug              (+ collision)
│   ├── level-ldtk         (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender      (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui
│       └── dialogue       (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision              (+ physics, soft)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

## block.json

The schema lives in [`block.schema.json`](./block.schema.json). Each
manifest declares only the metadata; the file list is **implicit** —
every file inside the block's directory (except `block.json` itself)
ships as part of the block.

| Field | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Kebab-case identifier, matches the directory name. |
| `description` | yes | One-line summary, shown by `monodreams list`. |
| `dependencies` | no | Other blocks required transitively. |
| `nugetDependencies` | no | `<PackageReference>` entries to inject into the user's csproj. |
| `csprojProperties` | no | Properties (e.g. `EnableDynamicLoading`) appended to the csproj. |
| `files` | no | **Override** the implicit-file-list. Useful only for blocks that ship files from outside their directory; most blocks omit this. |
| `mgcbEntries` | no | Lines appended to the user's Content pipeline `.mgcb`. |
| `postInstallNotes` | no | Markdown printed after install — for both humans and AI agents. |
| `agentsMd` | no | Path to an AGENTS.md snippet appended to the user's `AGENTS.md`. |
| `premisesRef` | no | Pointer into `docs/` so users can find the invariants this block obeys. |
| `demo` | no | Optional working demonstration. Files under `<block>/demo/` only ship with `--with-demo`. See "Block demos" below. |

### File copy convention

The CLI walks the block directory and copies every file at the same
relative path into the user's project. So `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs`
in this repo lands at `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs` in the user's
project. Namespaces stay aligned because C# namespaces are file-path
independent — the file at `MonoDreams/cursor/Component/CursorController.cs`
still declares `namespace MonoDreams.Component.Cursor`.

### Worked example

[`cursor/block.json`](./cursor/block.json) — the smallest
non-foundation block, depending on only `foundation` and `rendering`.
The block dir contains 7 source files; the manifest only carries the
metadata. Drift is impossible by construction: adding a file to the
directory makes it part of the block automatically.

## Block demos

A block can ship a runnable demonstration under `<block>/demo/`.
[`camera/demo/CameraDemoScreen.cs`](./camera/demo/CameraDemoScreen.cs)
is the reference. Conventions:

- Demo source lives in `<block>/demo/`. It is **excluded** from the
  core engine library (`MonoDreams.csproj` removes `**/demo/**` from
  its compile glob) and from `monodreams add <block>` by default.
- The host project [`MonoDreams.Demos`](../MonoDreams.Demos/) compiles
  every block's demo directly (`<Compile Include="..\MonoDreams\**\demo\**\*.cs">`)
  and exposes a launcher screen. Run with
  `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Demos`.
- The demo's entry class implements `IGameScreen`. Reuse
  `MonoDreams.Demos.UI.DemoUI` for menu chrome and
  `DemoButtonComponent` / `DemoButtonInteractionSystem` for clickable
  buttons that dispatch by id.
- Declare the demo in `block.json` via the `demo` field
  (`entry`, `description`, `dependencies`). The extra `dependencies`
  list captures blocks the demo needs over and above what the block
  itself requires (e.g. the `camera` demo declares `ui`, `cursor`,
  `rendering-text` for its menu chrome).

## Authoring a block

1. Create `MonoDreams/<name>/` and drop your source files in. Keep
   the block self-contained — anything that cuts across two blocks
   either belongs to a parent block or needs splitting.
2. Write `block.json` next to the code. Declare every dependency. The
   CLI fails loudly on a missing reference rather than guessing.
3. List any NuGet packages the source `using`s. The CLI injects them
   into the user's csproj at install time.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring*: which systems go where
   in the pipeline, what assets need to load, anything not derivable
   from reading the files.
5. Validate against `block.schema.json`.

## Validation

Any JSON Schema validator works. From the repo root with
[`ajv-cli`](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv-cli):

```bash
ajv validate -s MonoDreams/block.schema.json -d 'MonoDreams/*/block.json'
```

The CLI also runs validation before any install.

content.text:
I've got the lay of the land. "Block" is embedded in the manifest filename (`block.json`), the schema (`block.schema.json`), `BLOCKS.md`, the `BlockManifest` class, the registry/state JSON keys (`"blocks"`), and CLI help strings — so it's a mechanical-but-broad rename, not a deep one. Here's my take.

## Would I stick with "block"? No — your instinct is right.

Not because it's a bad word in the abstract, but because of a domain collision that's specific to *your* audience. shadcn borrowed "block" for a web crowd where the term is unloaded. In 2D gamedev, **"block" already means a thing on screen** — a tile, a piece of level geometry, a Minecraft/platformer block, a collidable object. You're even living that ambiguity already: "physics **block** demo: ten bouncing balls" reads as *a demo of physics blocks (objects)* at least as naturally as *the demo for the physics block (unit)*. That double meaning is exactly the friction you're sensing. For "the regular gamedev who just wants to build their game," the word points at the wrong mental model.

There's also a subtle mismatch with the source: in shadcn, the *atomic* unit is a "component" and a "block" is a larger composed section. You've inverted that — your atomic unit is the "block." So you don't even get the full benefit of the borrowed familiarity.

## The binding constraint

The reason this is hard: **`component`, `system`, `entity`, and `message` are all off the table** — they're core ECS vocabulary in this engine. That's almost certainly why "block" got picked in the first place (shadcn's own word, "component," would be catastrophic here). Any alternative has to dodge all four.

## Alternatives, ranked

| Term | Read | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **module** | "add the physics module" | **My top pick.** Honest description — a self-contained unit of source providing one capability with declared deps. Universally understood by devs, zero ECS collision, zero game-domain collision. Only nit: faintly implies "compiled/binary," which slightly undersells the you-own-the-source angle. |
| **kit** | "the dialogue kit" | **Best if you want warmth.** Hobbyist-gamedev-native ("starter kit," "toolkit"), friendly, approachable. Slight risk it implies a *bundle of many things* rather than one capability. |
| **feature** | "add the camera feature" | Maximum plain-English for your persona. But too generic to brand (`feature.json`? meh) and overloaded with product-speak. |
| **plugin** | "the collision plugin" | **Avoid, despite being the most instantly familiar.** "Plugin" signals a *runtime-loaded binary extension into a host app* (Unity/Godot/Unreal plugins) — the exact opposite of copy-the-source-and-own-it. It would actively teach users the wrong model, even though your existing "plug'n play" language flirts with it. |
| **block** (keep) | — | Works, has lineage, but collides with game geometry and is abstract. |

Honorable mention: **slice** — "vertical slice" is genuine gamedev jargon for a self-contained cut through the whole stack, which is conceptually perfect. But "vertical slice" specifically means *a playable demo build*, so it'd cross wires.

content.text:
Good instinct to want the ownership idea visible — but I'd **not bake it into the unit's name.** Make the noun `module`, and let "source" do its work in the *framing* around it. Here's the reasoning.

**A two-word unit name doesn't survive daily use.** This is the noun you'll type and say hundreds of times — CLI output, docs, issues, conversation. "Add the physics source module" gets clipped to "add the physics module" within a day, by you and by users, automatically. So the second word vanishes from speech and only lives in copy. If it only lives in copy, it shouldn't be load-bearing in the noun.

**"Source" belongs in the pitch, not the unit name — and that's exactly the shadcn playbook.** shadcn's unit is a "component," not a "source component." The entire "you own the code, it's not a dependency" philosophy lives in the *positioning* ("This is NOT a component library…"), not in the noun. They keep the noun short and hammer the ownership idea in the tagline and docs. You should do the same: `module` is the noun; "source modules you own" is the category descriptor.

**The mechanism sells ownership better than any adjective ever will.** The first time someone runs `monodreams add physics` and watches 8 `.cs` files land *in their own repo, under their own namespace, tracked by their own git, editable right there* — that lands the "not a blackbox" message harder than the word "source" possibly could. The CLI's behavior is the argument. "Source" in the name is a label trying to do what the tool already does for free.

**The one real merit of "source module":** it kills the faint binary connotation I flagged last turn — "module" can read as Python-module / .NET-assembly-module / NuGet-ish. "Source module" actively corrects that. That's a genuine point in its favor, and it's why "source" deserves to be *present somewhere prominent* — just not welded to the noun everywhere.

**Minor downside of the compound:** in C/C++ land "source module" already nods at translation-unit / source-file, and "a module of source code" is mildly redundant (most code is source). The distinction you actually want isn't "this is source" — it's "this is *yours to modify*," which "source" only weakly carries.

## What I'd do

Use **`module`** as the noun everywhere it's a noun, and use **"source module(s)"** as the category descriptor on first mention + in taglines. Concretely:

- **Tagline / first line of `BLOCKS.md` / README:** "MonoDreams ships as **source modules** — self-contained slices of engine code you copy into your project and own outright."
- **CLI banner:** keep "source" exactly where it already is — *"MonoDreams CLI — copies engine source modules into your project."*
- **Everywhere after first mention:** just "module." `module.json`, `monodreams add physics`, "the camera module depends on rendering."

So in practice:

> *"Each MonoDreams capability is a **source module** — you own every line. Run `monodreams add physics` and the **module**'s files land in your repo, yours to edit."*

First mention sets the ownership frame; the working noun stays one syllable's worth of friction lighter.

Net: `module`, with "source module" reserved as the intro framing — not `source module` as the literal name. Want me to run the `block → module` rename on that basis when you're ready?

# MonoDreams Modules

The engine ships as a set of **modules** — self-contained, copyable
slices of source code. Each module is a directory under `MonoDreams/`
with its own `module.json` manifest sitting next to the code it
describes. The `monodreams` CLI reads these manifests, resolves the
dependency graph, and copies the source into a user's project.

The model is **shadcn for C# game code**: nothing is hidden behind a
NuGet binary. The user owns every line; AI agents can read and edit
the code in place.

## Layout

```
MonoDreams/
  module.schema.json       ← JSON Schema validating every manifest
  presets.json            ← curated module combinations
  MODULES.md               ← this file
  MonoDreams.csproj       ← engine project (globs all module source)
  README.md, Icon.*       ← engine-only project assets
  Effect/                 ← engine-only shaders (not part of any module)
  <module>/
    module.json            ← the manifest
    ...source files...    ← all files inside ARE the module
```

The engine ships as a set of **modules** — self-contained, copyable
slices of source code. Each module is a directory under `MonoDreams/`
with its own `module.json` manifest sitting next to the code it
describes. The `monodreams` CLI reads these manifests, resolves the
dependency graph, and copies the source into a user's project.

NuGet binary. The user owns every line; AI agents can read and edit
the code in place.

  presets.json            ← curated module combinations
  MODULES.md               ← this file
  MonoDreams.csproj       ← engine project (globs all module source)
  README.md, Icon.*       ← engine-only project assets
  Effect/                 ← engine-only shaders (not part of any module)
  <module>/
    module.json            ← the manifest
    ...source files...    ← all files inside ARE the module
```

The 13 modules:

```
foundation              (required base — installed by `monodreams init`)
├── rendering            (includes mesh primitives — IMeshGenerator, MeshData)
│   ├── rendering-text
│   ├── camera
│   ├── cursor
│   ├── debug              (+ collision)
│   ├── level-ldtk         (+ level-loading)
│   ├── level-blender      (+ level-loading)
│   └── ui
│       └── dialogue       (+ rendering-text)
├── physics
├── collision              (+ physics, soft)
└── level-loading
    ├── level-ldtk
    └── level-blender
```

## module.json

The schema lives in [`module.schema.json`](./module.schema.json). Each
manifest declares only the metadata; the file list is **implicit** —
every file inside the module's directory (except `module.json` itself)
ships as part of the module.

| Field | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | yes | Kebab-case identifier, matches the directory name. |
| `description` | yes | One-line summary, shown by `monodreams list`. |
| `dependencies` | no | Other modules required transitively. |
| `nugetDependencies` | no | `<PackageReference>` entries to inject into the user's csproj. |
| `csprojProperties` | no | Properties (e.g. `EnableDynamicLoading`) appended to the csproj. |
| `files` | no | **Override** the implicit-file-list. Useful only for modules that ship files from outside their directory; most modules omit this. |
| `mgcbEntries` | no | Lines appended to the user's Content pipeline `.mgcb`. |
| `postInstallNotes` | no | Markdown printed after install — for both humans and AI agents. |
| `agentsMd` | no | Path to an AGENTS.md snippet appended to the user's `AGENTS.md`. |
| `premisesRef` | no | Pointer into `docs/` so users can find the invariants this module obeys. |
| `demo` | no | Optional working demonstration. Files under `<module>/demo/` only ship with `--with-demo`. See "Module demos" below. |

### File copy convention

The CLI walks the module directory and copies every file at the same
relative path into the user's project. So `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs`
in this repo lands at `MonoDreams/cursor/Cursor.cs` in the user's
project. Namespaces stay aligned because C# namespaces are file-path
independent — the file at `MonoDreams/cursor/Component/CursorController.cs`
still declares `namespace MonoDreams.Component.Cursor`.

### Worked example

[`cursor/module.json`](./cursor/module.json) — the smallest
non-foundation module, depending on only `foundation` and `rendering`.
The module dir contains 7 source files; the manifest only carries the
metadata. Drift is impossible by construction: adding a file to the
directory makes it part of the module automatically.

## Module demos

A module can ship a runnable demonstration under `<module>/demo/`.
[`camera/demo/CameraDemoScreen.cs`](./camera/demo/CameraDemoScreen.cs)
is the reference. Conventions:

- Demo source lives in `<module>/demo/`. It is **excluded** from the
  core engine library (`MonoDreams.csproj` removes `**/demo/**` from
  its compile glob) and from `monodreams add <module>` by default.
- The host project [`MonoDreams.Demos`](../MonoDreams.Demos/) compiles
  every module's demo directly (`<Compile Include="..\MonoDreams\**\demo\**\*.cs">`)
  and exposes a launcher screen. Run with
  `dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Demos`.
- The demo's entry class implements `IGameScreen`. Reuse
  `MonoDreams.Demos.UI.DemoUI` for menu chrome and
  `DemoButtonComponent` / `DemoButtonInteractionSystem` for clickable
  buttons that dispatch by id.
- Declare the demo in `module.json` via the `demo` field
  (`entry`, `description`, `dependencies`). The extra `dependencies`
  list captures modules the demo needs over and above what the module
  itself requires (e.g. the `camera` demo declares `ui`, `cursor`,
  `rendering-text` for its menu chrome).

## Authoring a module

1. Create `MonoDreams/<name>/` and drop your source files in. Keep
   the module self-contained — anything that cuts across two modules
   either belongs to a parent module or needs splitting.
2. Write `module.json` next to the code. Declare every dependency. The
   CLI fails loudly on a missing reference rather than guessing.
3. List any NuGet packages the source `using`s. The CLI injects them
   into the user's csproj at install time.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring*: which systems go where
   in the pipeline, what assets need to load, anything not derivable
   from reading the files.
5. Validate against `module.schema.json`.

## Validation

Any JSON Schema validator works. From the repo root with
[`ajv-cli`](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv-cli):

```bash
ajv validate -s MonoDreams/module.schema.json -d 'MonoDreams/*/module.json'
```

The CLI also runs validation before any install.

# Contributing to MonoDreams

Thanks for considering a contribution! MonoDreams is alpha and there's plenty of room to shape it. This doc covers what you need to build the engine, run the tests, and add a new module.

If you only want to *use* the engine for your own game, you don't need this file — see the project [README](./README.md) and the [`monodreams` CLI](./MonoDreams.Cli/).

## Prerequisites

- **.NET 8.0 SDK or newer** (the project uses `<RollForward>Major</RollForward>` so .NET 9/10 work too).
- **Python 3** for the registry-validation helpers (used by the schema check).
- A C# editor — Rider, VS, VS Code with C# Dev Kit, or `dotnet` from the command line.

### macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon)

```bash
# .NET 8 SDK via Homebrew (recommended for Apple Silicon)
brew install dotnet@8 freeimage

# Then add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bash_profile:
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet@8/bin:$PATH"
export DOTNET_ROOT="/opt/homebrew/opt/dotnet@8/libexec"

# Apple Silicon only: one-time MGCB FreeImage fixup after first restore
cp /opt/homebrew/lib/libfreeimage.dylib \
   ~/.nuget/packages/dotnet-mgcb/3.8.4/tools/net8.0/any/libFreeImage.dylib
```

Manual `~/.dotnet` install? Use `DOTNET_ROOT="$HOME/.dotnet"` instead.

### Windows

Install the .NET 8 SDK from <https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0>.

### Linux

Follow Microsoft's [Linux install guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/install/linux). MonoGame's MGCB content pipeline needs `libfontconfig1` and `libfreeimage3`.

## Building

```bash
# Clone and restore
git clone https://github.com/roo-oliv/monodreams.git
cd monodreams
dotnet tool restore
dotnet restore

# Build everything
dotnet build

# Run the example games
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Examples/MonoDreams.Examples.csproj

# Run the CLI from source
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Cli -- list
```

### Individual projects

```bash
dotnet build MonoDreams/MonoDreams.csproj            # core engine (all modules)
dotnet build MonoDreams.Examples/MonoDreams.Examples.csproj
dotnet build MonoDreams.Tests/MonoDreams.Tests.csproj
dotnet build MonoDreams.Cli/MonoDreams.Cli.csproj
```

## Tests

```bash
dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/
```

The integration tests use the **headless replay** harness in `MonoDreams.Tests/IntegrationTests/`. Each test writes an `InputReplayPlan`, spawns the example game in headless mode with a temporary debug directory, waits for it to exit, and asserts on the resulting log. See `GameTestRunner.cs` for the runner and the existing tests (LDtk, Blender, infinite-runner) for patterns.

## Repo layout

```
MonoDreams/                  ← the engine (15 modules + project files)
  module.schema.json          ← JSON Schema for every module.json
  presets.json               ← named module combinations
  MODULES.md                  ← module authoring guide
  MonoDreams.csproj          ← the engine library (compiles every module together)
  <module>/                   ← e.g. foundation/, rendering/, cursor/
    module.json               ← module manifest
    ...source files...       ← every file inside is part of the module
MonoDreams.Examples/         ← reference games (LDtk, Blender, infinite-runner)
MonoDreams.Cli/              ← the `monodreams` global tool (init / add / list)
MonoDreams.Tests/            ← integration + unit tests
docs/                        ← engine tenets and per-domain premises
.claude/                     ← Claude Code skills (e.g. /deep-review)
```

## Adding or modifying modules

The repo is the registry. To add a new module:

1. Create `MonoDreams/<name>/` and drop your source files there. The module dir defines its own contents — anything inside (except `module.json`) is shipped.
2. Write `MonoDreams/<name>/module.json`. Required fields are `name` and `description`; declare every cross-module dependency in `dependencies`. See [`MonoDreams/MODULES.md`](./MonoDreams/MODULES.md) for the full schema and [`MonoDreams/cursor/module.json`](./MonoDreams/cursor/module.json) for a small worked example.
3. List any new NuGet packages your source `using`s under `nugetDependencies` so the CLI injects them when users install your module.
4. Add `postInstallNotes` with the *wiring* — system pipeline order, asset hooks, anything not derivable from reading the files. Both humans and AI agents read these.
5. If the module touches an existing engine domain that has a `docs/<domain>/premises.md`, read the premises first (see [CLAUDE.md's workflow section](./.claude/CLAUDE.md#workflow)) and propose new premise text if your change introduces an invariant the docs don't yet name.

Validate the manifest:

```bash
# With ajv-cli
npx ajv-cli validate -s MonoDreams/module.schema.json -d 'MonoDreams/*/module.json'

# Or with the bundled Python helper (uses uv + jsonschema)
uv run --with jsonschema python3 -c "
import json, glob, jsonschema
schema = json.load(open('MonoDreams/module.schema.json'))
for p in sorted(glob.glob('MonoDreams/*/module.json')):
    jsonschema.validate(json.load(open(p)), schema)
print('all manifests valid')
"
```

End-to-end test the change:

```bash
# Regenerate a sandbox project via the CLI and build it
rm -rf .sandbox
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Cli -- init Sandbox --dir .sandbox/Sandbox
dotnet run --project MonoDreams.Cli -- add --preset infinite-runner --project .sandbox/Sandbox
dotnet build .sandbox/Sandbox/Sandbox.csproj
```

## Conventions

- **Components** end in `Component` (e.g. `TransformComponent`, `VelocityComponent`). They are pure data — no logic, no methods beyond simple constructors/helpers.
- **Systems** end in `System` (e.g. `HierarchySystem`, `GravitySystem`). All behavior lives in systems.
- **Messages** flow through the ECS world via publish-subscribe (e.g. `CollisionMessage`, `LoadLevelRequest`).
- **Namespaces are file-path independent.** A file at `MonoDreams/cursor/Component/CursorControllerComponent.cs` still declares `namespace MonoDreams.Component.Cursor`. This lets us reorganize files into module directories without breaking downstream code.
- **Core has no implicit `using`s.** When moving files in, add explicit `using System;`, `using System.Collections.Generic;`, `using System.Linq;` where needed.

## Engine invariants

Before any non-trivial change, read [`docs/CORE_TENETS.md`](./docs/CORE_TENETS.md). For each domain you touch, read the matching `docs/<domain>/premises.md` (rendering, hierarchy-transform, collision, physics, level-loading). Skipping these is the most common way changes silently break an engine contract.

## Coding style

Follow the existing code in the module you're editing — formatting, naming, comment density. The repo doesn't ship an `.editorconfig`-enforced style; the codebase's own consistency is the style guide.

## Skills

The repo's `.claude/skills/` directory contains Claude Code skills that help during contribution:

- `/deep-review` — multi-agent review of a PR or branch through six lenses calibrated for MonoDreams (adjacent-code, system-ordering, framework-fit, cross-domain deps, premises/test-coverage, ECS-purity). Invoke with `/deep-review <PR# or branch>`.

## Filing issues and PRs

- **Bugs** — include the reproduction, the expected vs actual behavior, and which modules are installed in your `monodreams.json`.
- **PRs** — make them focused; one module or one premise per PR is ideal. Update tests, premises, and `postInstallNotes` in the same PR that changes behavior.

## License

By contributing you agree your contributions are licensed under the [MIT License](./LICENSE).

# MonoDreams Project Memory

## Project Structure (Post-Refactor)
- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library with rendering, camera, cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading
- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific: screens, input, dialogue, layout, settings, entity factories

- **EntityInfo** is string-based in core (`new EntityInfo("Player")`), Examples has `EntityType` enum convenience

- When moving files: use `cp` + `sed` (not cat/heredoc) so user can cache permissions in Claude Code
- Always `sed -i ''` on macOS (BSD sed requires empty string for in-place editing)
- After moving files from Examples to core, check for empty directories and remove them
- Build after every phase to catch issues early
- The plan was organized into phases with commits per phase for bisectability

7 commits implementing the full core/Examples alignment refactoring.

description: Distributable units are "modules" (formerly "blocks") — naming decision, framing, and rename gotchas
metadata:
  type: project
---

The shadcn-style distributable units are called **modules**, not "blocks"
(renamed across the whole repo on branch `feat/packages`, 2026-06-15).

- The noun everywhere is **module**: `module.json`, `module.schema.json`,
  `MODULES.md`, `ModuleManifest`, CLI `Available modules (N)`, JSON keys
  `"modules"` in `presets.json` / registry index / state file.
- "**source module**" is the intro/category framing ONLY (first mention,
  taglines, CLI banner "copies engine source modules into your project") —
  emphasizes you own/edit the source, it's not a NuGet blackbox. Don't weld
  "source" onto the noun in daily use; "module" is the working term.
- **"component" / "system" / "entity" / "message" are off-limits** as the
  unit name — they're core ECS vocabulary. That constraint is why "block"
  was originally chosen and why "module" (not shadcn's own "component") is
  the replacement.

**Why:** the user judged "block" actively misleading for a gamedev audience
— in 2D gamedev "block" already means a tile / level-geometry / collidable
object, so it collided with the engine's own domain.
**How to apply:** never reintroduce "block" for a distributable unit. There
are exactly TWO legitimate game-sense "block" usages left in the source
(do not rename): `MonoDreams.Demos/UI/SproutIcons.cs` ("dark-tone block" =
spritesheet region) and `dialogue/demo/DialogueDemoScreen.cs` ("auto-tile
block" = tiling). The pipeline phase is "**stage**" (prep / cull / sort /
render stage), never "block" or "module".

**Rename gotcha (cost me a near-miss):** a global gitignore `debug/` rule
makes gitignore-aware tools (the harness `grep -r` / ripgrep) silently skip
`MonoDreams/debug/` even though it's a TRACKED source module (`.gitignore`
in-repo does NOT ignore it; git keeps tracking already-committed files). For
repo-wide find/replace, enumerate with `find`, not `grep -r`, or the whole
debug module is invisible. Same applies to `.sandbox/` (gitignored scratch,
has a stale `monodreams.json`) and `.entire/` (session metadata).

Related: [[module-demo-pattern]], [[dialogue-demo-notes]].

description: "Dialogue block wiring learned building its demo (in-memory Yarn, command-driven emotes)"

The `dialogue` block's `DialogueSystem` is a complete, self-contained UI driver: its
constructor builds the box + revealing-text + options + click-to-continue entities on the
UI target and runs the Yarn VM. You feed it `(World, dialogBoxTex, BitmapFont, indicatorTex,
vw, vh, layerDepth, interact, up, down, YarnProgram[], entityInfoType, textScale, sideInset,
indicatorSize)` and trigger it by publishing `DialogueStartMessage(entity, "NodeName")`.
Options are keyboard-driven (up/down + interact), rendered with a `> ` prefix. Line + option
text auto-word-wraps to the box width (`WrapText`, inserting `\n`; reveal slices the wrapped
string). `sideInset` reserves symmetric box side room for game-drawn portraits; `textScale`
(default 0.32, demo uses 0.3) and `indicatorSize` (default 44) were hardcoded before.

**In-memory Yarn (no .yarn asset needed):** `YarnProgram` is a plain container. Compile a
yarn string at runtime mirroring `YarnSpinnerProcessor.Process`: `CompilationJob.CreateFromString`
→ `Compiler.Compile` → write `result.Program` protobuf bytes to `CompiledProgram`, write
`result.StringTable` to `BaseLocalisationStringTable` CSV (cols id,text,file,node,lineNumber).
`Yarn.Compiler`/`Google.Protobuf`/`CsvHelper` flow transitively from MonoDreams (non-private
PackageRefs). Yarn line form is `Speaker: text` (DialogueSystem splits on the colon).

**Input:** DialogueSystem reads three `AInputState`s. Feed them with an
`AKeyboardInputHandlingSystem` subclass (InputMapping = [(interact,E),(up,Up),(down,Down)]),
run FIRST in the update pipeline. Share the SAME `interact` instance between the NPC trigger
and DialogueSystem — `StartYarnDialogue` calls `_interact.Consume()` so the opening press
doesn't also advance the first line. Add `TextUpdateSystem` to the UPDATE pipeline (the other
demos omit it) so the reveal animates; it only touches DynamicTextComponent, not transforms.

**Engine change made (branch feat/packages, uncommitted as of 2026-05-30):** `OnYarnCommand`
was a dead-end debug log. Now it publishes `DialogueCommandMessage(commandText)` and sets
`_pendingContinue`; `Update` does a deferred `Continue()` (NOT re-entrant inside the handler)
so inline `<<command>>` doesn't stall the line. `_pendingContinue` is reset in
`DeactivateDialogue`. Premises added to `dialogue/docs/premises.md` (commands + wrap/inset).

**Demo command layer (two systems, both subscribe to `DialogueCommandMessage`, dispatch by
verb):** `<<emote who kind>>` → `DialoguePortraitSystem`: a wood-brown framed Teemo face
*inside* the box (left=NPC, right=player), persists until the next emote / dialogue end.
`<<react who mark>>` → `ReactionMarkSystem`: an `all_icons` reaction sprite (`!`/`?`/star via
`SproutIcons`) *above* the character's head (Main target), auto-expires ~1.6s. The portrait is
demo-owned UI entities (frame = mesh, face = sprite) over the box's reserved `sideInset` zones;
hide on UI = clear the drawable (face `SpriteSheet`+`Texture`=null; frame mesh `Vertices`=null),
NOT toggle VisibleComponent. Reaction marks are Main children → toggle VisibleComponent.
NOTE: on UI, `SpritePrep`/`MeshPrep` still REQUIRE VisibleComponent (it's in their `[With]`) to
refill the drawable — so VisibleComponent is not a no-op on UI, it gates the prep.

**Round 3 fixes (branch feat/packages, uncommitted as of 2026-05-30):**
- **Text line-spacing is now an engine feature.** Wrapped lines overlapped because
  `MasterRenderSystem`'s text case passed the whole `\n` string to one `DrawString` and
  MonoGame.Extended's newline advance IGNORES the draw scale. Fix: `DynamicTextComponent`
  + `DrawComponent` gained a `LineSpacing` float (≤0 ⇒ 1.0); `TextPrepSystem` carries it;
  `MasterRenderSystem` now `Split('\n')` and draws one line per `Font.LineHeight*Scale.Y*
  LineSpacing`. Premise added in `rendering-text/docs/premises.md`.
- **Sampler is now per-draw-type in `MasterRenderSystem`.** Global `LinearClamp` blurred
  up-scaled pixel sprites (the 16×16 indicator → 48×48). Fix: `BatchType` split into
  Sprite/Text/Mesh; Sprite+Mesh→PointClamp (crisp), Text→LinearClamp (smooth downscaled
  fonts). Configurable via ctor `spriteSampler`/`textSampler` params (default to those).
  Premise added in `rendering/docs/premises.md`.
- **Cow-head NPC portrait:** `DialoguePortraitSystem` now takes a distinct sheet+source per
  side — NPC(left)=cow head crop (the cow faces RIGHT; head = right-center of frame (0,0),
  `Rectangle(13,2,18,18)`), player(right)=emote cells. The cow has no expression frames so
  `kind` is ignored for it.
- **Player portrait while choosing:** added `<<emote player question>>` before the option
  group in `YarnSource` — the deferred-continue fires it just before `OnYarnOptions`.
- **"E to talk" prompt was occluded by the header.** Camera centers world (0,0) on screen
  center; the cow at top-left had its head at the boundary top, so the above-head prompt
  landed above the field, under the header (UI composites over Main). Fix: moved NpcPosition
  down to (-300,-60) for headroom.

**Round 4 fixes (branch feat/packages, uncommitted as of 2026-05-31):**
- **Two-layer dialogue box is now an engine feature (balloon mode).** `DialogueSystem` gained
  optional params `talkBalloonTexture`, `talkBalloonNinePatch`, `portraitGutter`,
  `balloonPadding`, `boxHeight`, `boxNinePatch` (all default to legacy behavior). When a
  balloon texture is passed, it creates a 4th child (inner nine-patch panel at
  `_layerDepth+0.005`) and lays text/options/indicator INSIDE the balloon, reserving a left
  `portraitGutter` for a game-drawn emote frame; `sideInset` is ignored in this mode. Exposes
  `PortraitGutterBounds` (UI-space Rectangle) so the demo places its frame against the real
  layout. The balloon entity needs VisibleComponent toggled with the box (SpritePrep gates on
  it even on UI). `sideInset` vs `portraitGutter` overlap = flagged follow-up debt. Premise
  added in `dialogue/docs/premises.md` ("Balloon mode").
- **Default line leading is now 1.15** via `DynamicTextComponent.DefaultLineSpacing` (single
  const; TextPrepSystem + MasterRenderSystem resolve ≤0 to it; DrawComponent field default =
  it). `DialogueSystem.ShowOptions` MUST multiply its stacking lineHeight by DefaultLineSpacing
  or multi-line options overlap (done).
- **Sprout Lands UI pack imported:** `MonoDreams.Demos/Content/SproutLands/UI/basic_pack.png`
  (896×240, = "Sprite sheet for Basic Pack.png" from `~/Downloads/Sprout Lands - UI Pack -
  Basic pack/`; registered in Content.mgcb). Source rects used: dark-wood ornate emote frame
  `(153,105,30,30)` (rows at y9/57/105 = light/med/dark wood; interiors brown/mauve/purple);
  tan bg panel `(259,180,90,25)`; cream balloon panel `(163,178,90,27)`; nine-patch corner=8
  via `Panel9(rect,corner)` helper (corners 1:1, 1px edge/center strips stretched). KEY COLOR
  FACT: `dialog box medium` + beige panels are all `(232,207,166)`; the only distinct warm tone
  is the tan panel `(220,185,138)` — so a lighter-inner two-layer needs tan OUTER + cream
  (232) INNER (hence boxNinePatch + tan bg). Contrast is subtle; borders do the delineation.
- **Single emote frame.** `DialoguePortraitSystem` consolidated from left/right slots to ONE
  slot in the gutter; the wood frame is a static SPRITE now (was FilledRectangleMeshGenerator
  mesh); `ShowFace` swaps only the face (cow head for npc / emote cell for player — whoever
  speaks). Frame source `(153,105,30,30)` scaled 4×→120px; face 56px centred (foff 32).
- **Cow head crop reframed** `(13,2,18,18)`→`(14,12,16,16)` — lower+wider so the whole head
  (horns, both eyes, pink snout) is framed, not cut. Cow faces RIGHT, head in lower-right of
  the 32×32 frame (0,0). Verified by extracting/zooming candidate crops (PIL, no numpy).
- **Sprites integer-scaled:** `CowRenderSize 66→96` (3× of 32), `PlayerRenderSize 72→96` (2× of
  48) — crisp under PointClamp. `InteractRange 140→170`. Sidebar: dropped the "W walk around"
  row, "E" label → "Interact".
- Could NOT verify pixels (Demos host has no headless/screenshot path); built a PIL composite
  mock from the real assets at the computed geometry to sanity-check before the user runs it.

Related: [[block-demo-pattern]].

## Project Structure (Post-Refactor)
- `MonoDreams/` — core engine library with rendering, camera, cursor, collision, physics, entity spawning, level loading
- `MonoDreams.Examples/` — game-specific: screens, input, dialogue, layout, settings, entity factories
